hookups.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ ('Camping is primitive, temporary and dispersed. There are no established campsites and no amenities (electric, potable water, dump stations, restrooms, convenience stations).'), read 2026-10-21

facilities.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ ('no amenities (electric, potable water, dump stations, restrooms, convenience stations)'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Crooked Creek lists Primitive Camping among its activities; DWR: 'Two parking areas, one near the old concession building and another on the East Fork tract ... Additional parking is available along many sections of the stream.'

summary: Confirmed on DWR's Crooked Creek page that primitive camping is still allowed on the WMA, and from DWR's statewide camping page: no hookups, no water/dump/restrooms, 14-night limit, $10 camping authorization. Not stated: season (the fee-fishing season, first Saturday in April - Sept 30, is about fishing, not camping). Note left as is.
flags: Missing website: DWR's page for this WMA is https://dwr.virginia.gov/wma/crooked-creek/ (phone: DWR 804-367-1000, as on the other VA WMA entries).

Criteria lead: one of the two parking areas the inclusion evidence relies on is 'near the old concession building'; DWR's statewide rule says 'It is unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility (building, boat ramp, etc.)', so that lot may not be a legal camp spot if the building still stands. The East Fork lot and the stream-side pull-offs are not affected.
